To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the inductance of radiofrequency coils can be measured and that the inductances of flat-coils and of solenoids can be estimated with reasonable accuracy.
inductance can be accurately measured and estimated for radiofrequency NMM coils.

the inductance of flat-coils can be estimated using an empirical formula based upon coil dimensions, and the inductance for solenoids can be estimated using either an empirical formula based on coil dimensions or by using an equation based on coil dimensions and the permeability of the material in which the coil is embedded.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, construction and testing of NMR coils.
the design of radiofrequency coils for NMR.
the estimation and measurement of inductance of flat-coils and small solenoids, and with the practical application of this information in the design of NMR probes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the estimation of coil inductance is a difficult and often imprecise process and should be performed with care and with an understanding of the underlying physics of the process.
the measurement method is simple, straightforward and very accurate, and that the estimation methods are simple, straightforward and useful for the design of coils for use in solid-state NMR.
the inductance of radiofrequency coils can be accurately estimated using a number of different methods and that these estimates agree with the measured values to within a few percent.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
inductance estimation methods can provide useful information for coil design, and can be used as a guide for fabrication and testing of new coils for use in an existing NMR probe.
the use of inductance measurement circuits in the NMR laboratory provides a very useful and practical tool for coil design and optimization.
the use of the inductance measurement and estimation methods described herein is an effective and practical approach for coil design and optimization for solid-state NMR applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
inductance estimation is a useful technique for radiofrequency coil design and fabrication, especially for flat coils.
the inductance estimation formulae presented here can be used to estimate the inductance for flat or solenoid coils of any shape or size.
inductance estimation methods for flat coils and solenoids can be easily applied using instrumentation available in most NMR laboratories.
